title: PowerShell download-and-execute cradle
description: Detects PowerShell commands that combine a selected network download primitive with immediate expression execution.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use PowerShell to retrieve script content and execute it directly in memory.
hypothesis.rationale: MITRE documents PowerShell abuse, SigmaHQ maintains a comparable cradle analytic, and the authorized 30-day aggregate baseline was non-zero across several devices; legitimate automation therefore requires environment-specific review.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify PowerShell commands that combine a selected download primitive with IEX or Invoke-Expression while leaving download-only, execution-only, encoded-only and non-PowerShell commands unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Treat the match as a tuning-required hunting signal until its script source, execution context and observed non-zero baseline are explained.
steps: Review the complete command, decoded URL or source, account, parent process, device role and script host lineage.
Inspect downloaded content and correlate child processes, persistence, file writes, network connections and security-control changes.
Compare the activity with approved deployment or administration automation and add a narrowly scoped exception only after validating owner, source and purpose.
false_positives: Approved deployment, bootstrap, support or administration scripts that intentionally download and execute PowerShell content
Environment-specific automation represented in the non-zero authorized 30-day aggregate baseline and still requiring owner review

validation.expected_outcome: Match PowerShell commands combining selected download and expression-execution markers; do not match either behavior alone, another process or encoded-only PowerShell.
